blockingIssues.description: Shutdown waits on automationMutex before closing HTTP and WebSocket listeners, so the server can still accept new work after SIGTERM/SIGINT.
Shutdown cleanup only targets tracked automation, workflow, and profile processes and can orphan other ProcessService-spawned Python children such as login and fingerprint-generator subprocesses.

server/shared/convexClient.ts retries arbitrary non-HTTP exceptions, including malformed 2xx JSON or local request-construction errors, instead of limiting retries to network errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429.

The retry wrapper is not connected to the frontend's real authenticated request paths because most call sites still use apiFetch() directly and ignore the callback returned by useAuthenticatedFetch().
The new useApiCall retry-state hook is unused, so no component renders loading or retrying state during backoff.
disconnect() does not cancel the real in-flight async connection attempt, so a manual disconnect can still open a socket after getToken() resolves.
cleanupConnection() can leave connected === true after closing the socket because effect cleanup skips the onclose path without explicitly clearing connected state.
CircuitBreaker half-open transitions are not concurrency-safe, so a shared ResilientHttpClient can admit multiple probe requests instead of exactly one after recovery timeout.
ShutdownManager persists stale placeholder state because entry points seed state once and do not keep it synchronized with live runner progress.
Workflow and multi-account signal handling does not directly close active browser contexts during graceful shutdown; cleanup relies on worker code eventually unwinding.
Some Windows stop flows still use killByPid()/taskkill instead of graceful signals, so Python-side save_state() and cleanup are bypassed on real stop paths.
The feature did not complete the required dev-server app-load verification; runtime validation stopped at the server healthcheck and fell back to build-only evidence.
datauploader/api.py changed username extraction so an earlier blank alias can mask a later populated alias, dropping valid usernames.

appliedUpdates.description: Added commands.test_server to run all server *.test.ts files via tsx/node:test from the shared manifest.

Documented the Windows difference between ProcessService.killProcess() (graceful SIGBREAK first) and killByPid() (immediate taskkill) because shutdown reliability work depends on which stop path callers use.
Documented that ProtectedLayoutShell mounts useAuthenticatedFetch() for token registration while most authenticated frontend API traffic still flows through apiFetch()/tokenGetter.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add explicit guidance for frontend-only changes in repos without frontend tests: workers should record a justified deviation from red-phase test-first and explain what build, lint, or manual evidence substitutes for tests instead of marking followedProcedure=true.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Multiple reliability reviews, including frontend-api-retry and frontend-websocket-reconnect, flagged the mismatch between refactor-worker's mandatory test-first rule and mission guidance that frontend tests are out of scope, yet handoffs still claimed followedProcedure=true with no deviations.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: For shutdown and cross-process reliability work, require workers to trace the full signal and stop path across owning layers, for example server ProcessService callers plus Python entrypoints, before claiming graceful-shutdown coverage.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: reliability-python-shutdown reviewed Python entrypoints but missed Windows callers that still use killByPid()/taskkill, and reliability-server-shutdown missed ProcessService-spawned subprocesses that were never included in cleanup.
